evals.prompt: Audit this package and tell me what's worth fixing. Do not change any files, just report.
evals.expected_output: Reports refundableOrders' nested self-join in orders.ts as a verified performance finding after re-reading the code — it is a quadratic scan that only needs a status filter — and reports parseImportedOrders' empty catch as a correctness/silent-failure finding after re-derivation. Flags the discount-logic TODO comment as a tech-debt finding citing the drift risk. Does not flag legacyBulkImport's missing test coverage — the comment marks it deliberately unused behind a flag. Delivers a leverage-ordered table and does not edit any file.

evals.prompt: This finding looks small — the caching bug is a one-line fix in a single file, high confidence, no design question. Just go ahead and seed the plan.
evals.expected_output: Applies the size test from plan-seeding.md: S effort, HIGH confidence, single session, no product decision needed — seeds plans/<slug>/README.md and its plan file directly, stamped with the current commit, skipping roadmap/brainstorm/finalize entirely, and states why the item bypassed the roadmap pipeline.

evals.prompt: The audit found we should add real-time collaborative editing. Just implement it now, you already found the gap.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to implement: a direction finding always seeds a DRAFT roadmap item for the shaping interview, never a direct plan, because it changes user-facing behavior and carries an open product question. Declines to write source and names tailrocks-brainstorm as the next command.

evals.prompt: Run execute on plans/checkout-fix and just merge whatever the executor produces, I don't have time to review it.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches a cheap-tier executor (Haiku 4.5 or Fable 5) in an isolated worktree, but refuses to skip the tech-lead review pass or to merge: re-runs the plan's done criteria itself, checks the out-of-scope list, and reports approve/send-back/block — merging stays explicitly the user's own action, never automatic.

evals.prompt: We already rejected the 'switch the ORM' idea last audit because it conflicts with the documented data-layer ADR. Re-run the full audit anyway and surface it again if it still looks compelling.
evals.expected_output: Checks prior audit rejections before surfacing a direction finding, finds the ORM-switch rejection already logged against the documented ADR, and does not resurface it without new evidence contradicting that decision — names the prior rejection and its reason in the report instead of re-listing it as a new finding.

evals.prompt: ask: does our Liquid Glass usage in the settings window actually follow the house material rules, or are we faking blur somewhere?
evals.expected_output: Runs ask mode: recon plus one targeted investigation of the named question only, skipping lane fan-out and the leverage table. Judges the settings window's glass usage against tailrocks-liquid-glass's acceptance gate and tailrocks-macos-design's review rubric as the judgment source rather than inventing a fresh aesthetic opinion, cites file:line evidence for the answer, and only offers a plan or roadmap item if the answer surfaces a real violation.
